events.text: Orbs in repo
Are the orbs in my repo?

Yes, but only in `sonny914/new`. They aren't in `sonny914.github.io`.

**In `sonny914/new`:**
- `assets/orb/engine.js` (883 lines) is the orb engine.
- `assets/orb/thinking-orb.js` (287 lines) is the thinking-orb component, written without React.
- `lab/thinking-orb/index.html` is the lab page that shows it.
- `tools/orb.test.mjs` (133 lines) holds the tests.

The last two commits on those files are "Thinking orb: the thinking-orbs component without React" and "Thinking orb: grab it, fling it, tune it". That second one means you can grab and fling the orb, and adjust its settings.

**In `sonny914.github.io`:** there's no orb code. None of the site's JS or HTML mentions orbs. Some PNG/MP4 files under `docs/` came up in the search, but those were accidental matches inside the files' binary data, not orb assets.

If you want the orb on the live site, it has to be ported over from `new`. I can do that and put it on `claude/orbs-in-repo-68l8w7`.
I want to port that to my website under experiments. Also I need you to make . A 15 second reel highlighting showcasing the orbs features. Go all out. Show what you can do

events.text: #20 Lab 002: Thinking orb moves to /experiments, with a 15-second reel

The orb now has its own page on your site at `/experiments/thinking-orb/`, and the reel is done and sent above. It's all in draft PR #20: https://github.com/sonny914/new/pull/20

Your live site is the `new` repo (quietbands.com), so that's where this went. `sonny914.github.io` only holds design docs and screenshots, and I didn't touch it.

**On the site:**
- **Experiments section:** "Experiments" already exists as a section of your R&D page (`/rd/#experiments`). The orb is listed there as **Lab 002**, above Spatial Hero, with a small live orb next to the heading.
- **The orb's page** has the reel at the top, then the "Hold one" playground with every setting, all nine states, and a short write-up of how it works.
- **Links:** `quietbands.com/experiments` now goes to that section, so the URL on the reel's last frame works. The old `/lab/thinking-orb/` page is deleted and its address forwards to the new page.

**The reel:** 15 seconds, vertical 1080×1920, with its own soundtrack. Every frame is drawn by the real orb code, so nothing in it is a mock-up.
- An orange dot blooms into the orb.
- All nine states cut on the beat.
- They collapse into a 3×3 grid with an orange ripple: "Nine states. One engine."
- A hand grabs the orb, spins it and flings it, and it slows down the same way it does when you fling it on the page.
- "Tune it." The settings sliders move live and the color switches to orange.
- The 20px orb inside a "Sending…" button, then "Hold one." and the URL.
- The last frames fold back into the opening dot, so it loops without a visible cut on Reels and TikTok.

To change it later, edit `tools/reel/orb-reel.html` and run `node tools/reel/render.mjs`. A re-render takes about 30 seconds.

Tests pass (65/65). Both pages load cleanly on phone and desktop widths in a headless browser. Nothing has been checked on a real phone yet.

**Honest take:** the reel is strong content for @flighty.builds. It makes a code experiment look good, and that's the recognition you want. But it doesn't earn you anything by itself. Post it, and link it to the studio's work rather than to the orb itself.

Do you want me to watch the PR and handle any review comments or deploy failures?
Captions and hashtags

Merge PR #20 before you post. The end card and these captions point to quietbands.com/experiments, and that link won't work on the live site until the PR is deployed.

Credit Jakub Antalik, who wrote the open-source orb you built on, in every post, and tag him. I don't know his handles, so look them up rather than guessing. The builder crowd will spot an uncredited port, and that would undo the recognition you're posting for.

**Instagram Reels (@flighty.builds)**
```
Loading spinners just say "wait." This one tells you what kind of work is happening.

9 states. Searching scans a globe. Connecting wires up a constellation. Solving scrambles, then clicks back into place.

And you can grab it. Hold it, spin it, fling it, and it coasts back to its own pace.

Plain canvas. No React. No build step. Built on Jakub Antalik's open-source thinking-orbs.

Play with it → link in bio

#creativecoding #webdev #uidesign #microinteractions #buildinpublic
```
Pin this as the first comment:
```
Credit: the orb geometry is Jakub Antalik's thinking-orbs (MIT). I ported it off React and made it grabbable. Every frame of this reel was drawn by the real engine, nothing animated by hand.
```

**TikTok**
```
a loading spinner you can actually grab. 9 states, zero React. which one goes in your app? #creativecoding #webdev #uidesign #javascript #buildinpublic
```
The question at the end is there to get comments.

**X**
```
Loading spinners say "wait." This one shows what kind of work is happening, and you can grab it and fling it.

9 states, plain canvas, no React. Built on [Jakub's handle]'s thinking-orbs.
```
Put `quietbands.com/experiments/thinking-orb/` in the first reply, not the post itself. Posts with links tend to get less reach. Use one hashtag at most, or none.

**LinkedIn (Quiet Bands voice)**
```
Most loading indicators promise that something is happening. We wanted one that shows what kind of thing.

Lab 002 from Quiet Bands R&D: nine states, each a small piece of geometry that turns while the wait lasts. A globe scanned for searching. A constellation wiring itself for connecting. Bands that scramble and click back for solving.

It's Jakub Antalik's open-source thinking-orbs, taken off React onto plain canvas, with one addition: you can pick it up. Hold it and it stops. Drag it and it turns. Let go and it coasts back to its own pace.

It already runs on our intake form. The reel was drawn by the same engine, frame by frame.

Hold one: quietbands.com/experiments/thinking-orb/

#UXDesign #FrontendDevelopment #CreativeCoding
```

**Other first lines to test:**
- "I made the loading spinner grabbable."
- "A loading state you can hold."
- "Your loading spinner has one job. This one has nine."

**Hashtags to swap in:** #creativecoding #webdev #uidesign #uxdesign #microinteractions #frontend #javascript #motiondesign #generativeart #designengineering #indiehacker. Use 3–5 per post. More than that doesn't help reach and looks spammy.

This reel will mostly reach developers and designers, not people who'd hire the studio. That makes it good for @flighty.builds and the community you're growing there. The LinkedIn version is the only one with a realistic chance of reaching someone who pays, so that's the one to polish.

#20 merged into main

PR #20 is merged into `main`. Netlify publishes `main` automatically, usually within a couple of minutes. This environment's network blocks quietbands.com, so I couldn't load the live pages. What I did confirm is that `main` now has the orb page, the reel and the redirects.

Once the deploy finishes, these should work:
- `quietbands.com/experiments` takes you to the Experiments section of the R&D page, with the orb as Lab 002 at the top.
- `quietbands.com/experiments/thinking-orb/` is the orb page, with the reel, the playground and all nine states.
- `quietbands.com/lab/thinking-orb/` now forwards to the new page.

If they still show the old site after about five minutes, check the Deploys tab for the quietbands project in Netlify.

One mistake of mine went in with it: a 2.6MB sound file left over from building the reel (`tools/reel/out-sound.wav`). Visitors can't reach it, because the site blocks everything under `/tools/`, but it's clutter in the repo. Want me to remove it?
Yes
